response.sql: SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) as avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) as avg_HCT FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.ID IN (SELECT DISTINCT l2.ID FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.`U-PRO` = '-' AND l2.`RA` = '-') GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL, AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The '-' character in the request refers to the literal string '-' stored in U-PRO and RA columns, not any other representation (empty string, null, etc.)
SQL's AVG() function is used for calculating averages, which automatically excludes NULL values as requested by 'ignoring missing values'
